title: Balancing Pipeline Parallelism with Vocabulary Parallelism
problem: In pipeline-parallel LLM training, embedding and output vocabulary layers placed on one pipeline stage cause severe computation and memory imbalance, worsening pipeline bubbles and memory bottlenecks especially for large vocabularies.
method: Vocabulary Parallelism (VP) partitions embedding and output projection layers evenly across all pipeline devices. Computations are grouped into vocabulary-specific pipeline passes. Algorithm 1 reduces cross-device all-reduce barriers from 3 to 2; Algorithm 2 further reduces to 1 barrier by combining online softmax with pre-computed partial gradients. VP integrates with existing 1F1B and V-Half pipeline schedules via a generalizable method.

title: ReGate: Enabling Power Gating in Neural Processing Units
problem: Modern NPU chips (e.g., Google TPU generations) waste 30-72% of their active energy on static (leakage) power because they lack fine-grained power management support; conventional CPU/GPU power-gating techniques do not transfer directly because NPUs use large systolic arrays with deterministic dataflows, software-managed SRAM scratchpads, in-order VLIW pipelines, and no dynamic instruction scheduling.
method: ReGate uses hardware-software co-design differentiated by component. For systolic arrays (SAs): non-zero weight detection generates row/column bitmaps (col_nz, row_nz), and a prefix-sum circuit derives which rows/columns should be powered off; PE-level power gating then follows the diagonal weight-stationary dataflow — the PE_on signal propagates diagonally from the SA input, overlapping wake-up with computation to expose only single-PE wake-up latency. For ICI and HBM controllers: a lightweight hardware-based idle-detection state machine gates these units between collective operators (AllReduce, AllGather). For vector units and SRAM: a new NPU ISA extension adds setpm instructions with three modes (on/auto/off) that let the ML compiler insert power-management instructions at statically-known idle boundaries — the compiler determines VU idle gaps from instruction scheduling and SRAM capacity from tile-size analysis.

title: SampleAttention: Near-Lossless Acceleration of Long Context LLM Inference with Adaptive Structured Sparse Attention
problem: Long-context LLM prefill (TTFT) latency scales quadratically with sequence length due to dense attention computation; existing sparse attention methods use either static sparse patterns or fixed sparsity budgets, failing to adapt to per-head, per-input, and per-model variability in sparsity ratio and pattern. Both dimensions—optimal sparsity ratio and the exact structure of important tokens—must be determined dynamically at runtime to avoid accuracy loss.
method: SampleAttention introduces a two-stage query-guided key-value filtering algorithm driven by a new accuracy proxy called Cumulative Residual Attention (CRA), defined as the minimum fraction of attention probability mass retained per query after sparsification. Stage 1 (Query-Guided Chunked Sampling) partitions queries into chunkn equal segments, computes full attention scores for a small query block at the tail of each chunk, then reduces these token-level scores at block granularity (block size 128) along both column and slash directions. Stage 2 (Score-Based Key-Value Filtering) independently selects the minimum number of column-strip blocks and slash-strip blocks needed to satisfy separate CRA thresholds (αc, αs) via cumulative-sum top-k, extends the selected block indices to cover the full attention matrix, merges them into a binary block-sparse mask, and executes sparse FlashAttention2 on the result. Hardware efficiency is achieved by kernel-fusing the sampling pipeline (bmm, mask_fill, softmax, reduction) and by operator fusion for sequences >256K. Hyperparameters are tuned offline per model and per sequence-length range on a small RULER subset.

title: PIM Is All You Need: A CXL-Enabled GPU-Free System for Large Language Model Inference
problem: LLM inference is memory-bound (GEMV-dominated decoding stage with ~21% GPU compute utilization on Llama2-70B), yet modern GPU/TPU systems are optimized for compute throughput; simultaneously, large KV-cache requirements per user limit batch sizes, and CXL- or DRAM-density-reduced PIM architectures individually lack sufficient memory capacity or scalability for trillion-parameter LLMs.
method: CENT (CXL-ENabled GPU-Free sysTem) uses a hierarchical PIM-PNM architecture deployed across 32 CXL devices interconnected via a CXL 3.0 switch. Each CXL device contains 16 GDDR6-PIM memory chips (two PIM channels each) housing near-bank MAC reduction-tree processing units (16 MAC units/PU, BF16, 32 GFLOPS/PIM channel), plus PNM units including 32 accumulators, 32 reduction trees, 32 Taylor-series exponent accelerators, and 8 BOOM-2-wide RISC-V cores for non-MAC operations. MAC operations (>99% of arithmetic) execute near-bank; Softmax, RMSNorm, square root, and RoPE are handled by PNM. A custom CXL ISA (MAC_ABK, WR_GB, SEND_CXL, BCAST_CXL, etc.) orchestrates computation and data movement. LLM parallelism is implemented via pipeline parallel (PP: each transformer block to one CXL device, multiple prompts pipelined) and tensor parallel (TP: transformer block partitioned across all devices using broadcast/gather over CXL) mappings, with hybrid TP-PP for QoS balance. The CXL protocol is extended with a broadcast primitive via a reserved H-slot header code in port-based routing flits.

title: TurboAttention: Efficient Attention Approximation for High Throughput LLMs
problem: LLM attention is a dominant inference bottleneck at long context lengths: KV cache consumes massive memory, FlashAttention requires FP16/FP32 (using slow CUDA cores for softmax exponentiation), and existing KV cache compression methods still dequantize to FP16 before attention, negating latency benefits.
method: TurboAttention combines two innovations: (1) FlashQ — blockwise progressive quantization (BPQ) of Q/K/V to INT8 for FlashAttention-compatible quantized MatMuls, then channel-wise asymmetric INT4/INT2 compression of K/V for cache storage; headwise mixed precision assigns 2-bit quantization to the lowest-priority heads (based on a gap×std priority metric) and 4-bit to the rest. An enhanced KV buffer defers progressive compression every nb=64 steps. (2) SAS (Sparse Activated Softmax) — approximates exponentiation via LUT (integer part) + degree-3 polynomial (decimal part), runs entirely on Tensor Cores in FP16, and sparsifies near-zero attention scores to zero. Together these enable fully INT8 MatMul + FP16 softmax on Tensor Cores.
